title: Choose the look for your expense tracker
question: The roll assigned The Passbook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Passbook
options.lineage: Japanese bank passbooks (通帳), printed line by line at the ATM
options.thesis: Each month is a passbook page: purchases print oldest to newest, and a running total column climbs like a balance.
materials: BIZ UDPGothic, the face of Japanese forms
options.viewport: Cover-green rail with the months, oldest at the top; the month page fills the rest: total set large, then the printed rows with a running-total column, and the entry line waiting at the bottom where the next row prints.
options.risk: Oldest-first rows mean the newest purchase sits at the bottom of a long month; the page must open scrolled to the entry line.

raised.raise: Month navigation is one rail, the only moving part; everything else holds still.
The passbook's columns are the layout grid: every figure on the screen aligns to them.
Cover green appears only where something can be done; vermilion only where something is removed.
Three type sizes in total; rank is carried by weight and by the one reversed total row.

options.label: The Kakeibo
options.lineage: kakeibo (家計簿), the Japanese household account book, kept by week
options.thesis: The month is a kakeibo spread: purchases grouped by week, each week closing with its own subtotal.
materials: white page with blue week bands
options.viewport: Indigo top bar with month tabs; the page shows week blocks side by side in reading order, each with its rows and a subtotal band, the month total pinned at the right.
options.risk: Week blocks split a batch of entries across columns, and stationery-journal styling is a familiar look that can turn cute.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, one bright colour only where you can press.
options.viewport: One column of rounded cards with a bottom tab bar.
options.case: Built for thumbs; you enter batches on a laptop, and cards bury the table you scan.
options.risk: Wastes a laptop screen on padding.
options.kept: Action colour reserved strictly for things you can press.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Page
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail of keys, notes hung in the margin.
options.viewport: Twin columns with a vermilion key rail between them.
options.case: A reading layout; expenses are figures to enter and scan, not prose.
options.kept: One moving part: the month rail.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: A poster of giant grid-built figures.
options.case: A poster, not a tool; the grid would decorate rather than organise.
options.kept: The grid is the armature every figure aligns to.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal on raked glass slides.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides on a lit goldenrod bed.
options.case: The rake and lateral travel fight a table you scan top to bottom.
options.kept: Rank by weight and reversal, not by piling on sizes.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: A giant glyph morphing under a slider.
options.viewport: One giant letter and a glyph grid.
options.case: Nothing in your spending maps to a type axis.
options.kept: One number set at enormous scale against small figures.

options.label: Vertical Media Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the screen; the next is one flick away.
options.case: One purchase per screen is the opposite of reviewing a month.
options.kept: The current month owns the screen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean finance dashboard: white, sidebar, summary cards, blue accent, a sortable table.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, four summary cards across the top, the expense table below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every budgeting app by design.
